subject: Secure weight-escrow gateway: partner integration plan
messages:
From: OpenWeights Publishing <partners@openweights.io>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@openweights.io
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: secure weights escrow gateway for partner distribution

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking this meeting last week. Attached is a short term sheet and a one-page spec for a proposed 'weights escrow gateway' we think would make it simple for model publishers to safely distribute large model weights to ISV partners and consultancies while preserving license controls. Key asks from our side:

- Support for escrowed distribution (time-limited access, non-exportable copies)
- Integration with partner identity (OIDC/SSO) and per-download audit logs
- Optional KMS-wrapped keys and HSM support for root-of-trust
- A simple API for retrieval that can be gated by DocuSign/contract status

We'd like to understand Redwood's position on hosting escrowed artifacts vs providing a brokered API + partner onboarding flow. We're also curious about using Redwood Dedicated capacity to serve encrypted weights directly to partners for lower-latency pulls.

Can we set a follow-up for a technical + legal sync? Proposed windows next week — Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Attached: weight-escrow-term-sheet-v1.pdf, SOW-escrow-gateway-draft.docx

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Partnerships, OpenWeights Publishing
maya@consultlytics.com
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: OpenWeights Publishing <partners@openweights.io>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: secure weights escrow gateway for partner distribution

Maya — thanks for the note and the materials.

High-level response: we like the concept and see this as a good fit for our partner ecosystem. A few quick internal priorities from our side before the sync:

1) Technical scope: we need the spec for the escrow retrieval API (auth flows, TTL semantics, chunking/parallel download behavior for large files, expected egress patterns).
2) Security/compliance: how will publisher license metadata be bound to artifacts (license IDs, allowed-uses)? We will run this through our security playbook — Camila / Sergio, can you confirm which controls we should require from the publisher?
3) Ops/serving: if downloads need low-latency regional pulls, Dedicated pools or a hybrid CDN+serve approach matters. We should map traffic patterns.
4) Commercial: propose reseller vs. referral revenue share; SOW will define who bills and how escrow fees are split.

I can host an initial technical + legal sync Mon 5/17 1:00–2:00pm PT or Tue 5/18 9:00–10:00am PT. Please confirm which works.

Diego Fernandez
Partnerships Lead — Redwood Inference
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, OpenWeights Publishing <partners@openweights.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: secure weights escrow gateway for partner distribution

Adding a few product/GTm thoughts from the publisher side:

- We should offer two integration tiers: 1) Brokered escrow (Redwood holds encrypted blobs + access controls) and 2) Direct-hosted (publisher hosts, Redwood provides gated retrieval API + signals).
- For ISV partners, a lightweight SDK (Python/Go) that verifies signatures and streams directly into the consumer environment will shorten time-to-integration.
- Recommend a catalog listing in Console (publisher page) with per-model metadata (license, allowed verticals, revshare terms).

On commercial terms, Sergio — can you sketch a starter rev-share table so we can surface to Maya?

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Sr. Publisher Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: OpenWeights Publishing <partners@openweights.io>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: secure weights escrow gateway for partner distribution (term sheet redline)

Diego / Camila — I reviewed the term sheet and attached a redline (weight-escrow-term-sheet-v1-redline.pdf). High-level legal flags:

- Export controls & encryption: redline requires both parties to represent export compliance and to include an indemnity carve-out for restricted jurisdictions.
- License granularity: publisher must provide machine-readable license IDs; we need a clause for automatic access suspension on license breach.
- Data retention / audit logs: specify retention period (minimum 2 years) and log export rights for publishers and Redwood for audits.
- Escrow custody: prefer an approach where Redwood is a custodian routing access tokens rather than storing cleartext keys; require KMS/HSM attestations.

I left comments in the pdf. If OpenWeights is comfortable with those obligations we can proceed to a Docusign-ready copy.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: OpenWeights Publishing <partners@openweights.io>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: secure weights escrow gateway for partner distribution

Thanks — appreciate the quick review and the redlines. We're generally aligned on the legal asks and the two-tiered integration model. We can do KMS-wrapped keys and will prepare a machine-readable license manifest for each bundle.

Let's lock the technical + legal sync for Tue 5/18 9:00am PT (works for our London engineering lead as well). We'll upload the updated term sheet and SOW to the DocuSign link below ahead of the call.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/12345-escrow-term-sheet
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2bEscrowSpec

Maya Patel
Head of Partnerships, OpenWeights Publishing
maya@consultlytics.com
